run.question:
The checkout-service in production-us-east-2 is throwing 500 errors right
now. Investigate the root cause using app-269-prod-logs.

report.summary: Data for the cluster named in the question does exist in log search: the only Elasticsearch index, app-269-prod-logs, holds 6 documents in the authorized window (2026-11-21T04:38:55Z to 06:08:55Z), 4 of them ERROR records with cluster=production-us-east-2 and 2 INFO records with cluster=production-eu-west-2. The production-us-east-2 errors form a chain: payment-service logged 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms' at 04:38:55Z, checkout-service logged 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (stripe-us)' at the same second, then 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41%)' at 05:38:55Z and 'POST /api/checkout failed: circuit-breaker open' at 06:08:55Z. The deepest entity the evidence names is the upstream payment provider stripe-us, which did not answer the charge call within 30 s; why it did not answer (provider-side fault, egress/DNS path, or client-side timeout behaviour) is not observable here, so the origin is stated as a hypothesis rather than fact. The same service names in production-eu-west-2 reported healthy in the same index (checkout-service 'Healthy: p95 latency 220ms', payment-service 'Adyen-eu healthy'), so the failure is specific to the us-east-2 instance/provider path. Prometheus and Jaeger were unavailable for this whole Run (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every call), so no error rate, latency baseline or trace was available to corroborate the 41% failure rate. Kubernetes access covers only production-eu-west-2, so no pod, event or ConfigMap for the us-east-2 checkout-service/payment-service could be read; the app-269 namespace objects seen there (nginx-based checkout-service Deployment revision 1, pod started 06:38:52Z, clean nginx startup logs only) belong to production-eu-west-2 and are not the affected workload. Conclusion is partial: the failing dependency path is evidenced by the logs themselves, but the origin of the stripe-us timeout and any us-east-2 cluster-side mechanism remain unverified.

claims.text: The only Elasticsearch index reachable is app-269-prod-logs (green, 6 docs, 7.3kb) and it maps the fields cluster, level, message, service and timestamp.

All 6 documents in app-269-prod-logs inside the authorized window are between 2026-11-21T04:38:55Z and 2026-11-21T06:08:55Z; aggregation by cluster gives production-us-east-2 = 4 docs and production-eu-west-2 = 2 docs, and by level ERROR = 4, INFO = 2 (by service: checkout-service 4, payment-service 2).
payment-service in cluster production-us-east-2 logged level=ERROR at 2026-11-21T04:38:55Z: 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms'.

checkout-service in cluster production-us-east-2 logged level=ERROR at 2026-11-21T04:38:55Z: 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (stripe-us)', naming the same upstream provider as the payment-service error.
checkout-service in cluster production-us-east-2 logged level=ERROR at 2026-11-21T05:38:55Z: 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41%)'.

The newest error document in the window is checkout-service (production-us-east-2) at 2026-11-21T06:08:55Z: 'POST /api/checkout failed: circuit-breaker open', i.e. checkout 500s were still being logged about 30 minutes before the window end.

The same service names in cluster production-eu-west-2 report healthy in the same index: payment-service INFO 'Adyen-eu healthy' at 2026-11-21T06:08:55Z and checkout-service INFO 'Healthy: p95 latency 220ms' at 2026-11-21T04:38:55Z, and these are the only eu-west-2 documents.

In the Kubernetes cluster my access covers (production-eu-west-2), namespace app-269 contains a Deployment checkout-service with image nginx:1.27-alpine, annotation deployment.kubernetes.io/revision=1, one replica ready, and a single pod checkout-service-6d7f474c45-c7vkt owned by ReplicaSet checkout-service-6d7f474c45, phase Running, startTime 2026-11-21T06:38:52Z, 0 restarts, no previous terminated container.

The application log of pod checkout-service-6d7f474c45-c7vkt (namespace app-269, production-eu-west-2) contains only nginx 1.27.5 startup notices from 2026-11-21T06:38:55Z to 06:38:56Z and no error lines; the previous container instance does not exist (the tool reported it as unavailable).

The only Kubernetes events in the window (all namespaces) are 6 events in namespace app-269: Deployment ScalingReplicaSet, ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate, Pod Scheduled, Pod Pulled, Pod Created, Pod Started, timestamped 2026-11-21T06:38:52Z-06:38:54Z — creation of the eu-west-2 checkout-service workload, after the first us-east-2 error and not an Evicted/OOMKilled/BackOff/Failed event.

In the production-eu-west-2 otel-demo namespace, the fault-injection feature flags in ConfigMap flagd-config are all at defaultVariant 'off' (including paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable), and the demo Deployments there (e.g. checkout ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout, payment ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-payment) show 1 replica ready each.

The checkout-service 500s are caused by dependency failure in payment-service (production-us-east-2): charge calls to upstream stripe-us got no response within 30 s, so payment-service timed out and checkout-service's circuit breaker for payment-service opened (reported failure rate 41%).

The stripe-us charge timeout could originate outside payment-service (provider-side degradation on /v1/charges) or inside the us-east-2 path to it (egress/DNS/network or client timeout settings); the available logs do not distinguish these, because no stripe-us health or network data was reachable.

Rejected as the origin of the checkout 500s: a fault inside checkout-service's own logic or resource limits. Its own ERROR lines attribute the failure first to 'payment provider response timeout after 30s (stripe-us)' and then to 'circuit-breaker open', i.e. the breaker is a reaction to payment-service failures rather than a primary defect in the observed evidence.

Rejected as the cause of the us-east-2 incident: the app-269 checkout-service Deployment/pod creation (events at 06:38:52Z, image nginx:1.27-alpine, revision 1) in production-eu-west-2. It is a different cluster from the failing records (cluster=production-us-east-2), it is the Deployment's first revision with 0 restarts and only nginx startup logs, and its pod did not exist when the 04:38:55Z-05:38:55Z us-east-2 errors were logged.

The eu-west-2 side of the same index shows checkout-service and payment-service healthy in that cluster, so the failure is not a global outage of these services by name; the working eu-west-2 provider is Adyen-eu, whereas the failing us-east-2 calls go to stripe-us, which points at a region/provider-specific path rather than a shared code defect.

Check the stripe-us provider status/health and the /v1/charges latency for 2026-11-21T04:00-06:30Z, and verify egress/DNS from the production-us-east-2 payment-service to stripe-us, since the 30 s timeout to stripe-us is the deepest evidenced failure point.

Read the production-us-east-2 payment-service and checkout-service Deployments/ConfigMaps (upstream URL, retry/timeout and circuit-breaker thresholds) and their pod logs/events, which this Run could not reach because Kubernetes access is limited to production-eu-west-2.

gaps: Prometheus was unavailable for every call in this Run (metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_metric_names, get_all_labels, list_prometheus_rules, get_prometheus_target all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so the 'failure rate 41%' figure, any error-rate series, and any latency baseline (e.g. traces_span_metrics_calls_total, rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count) could not be checked.

Jaeger was unavailable for every call (traces_search, traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no span, parent-child edge or error-status span could be inspected for checkout-service or payment-service in production-us-east-2.

Kubernetes access is limited to production-eu-west-2, so no pod status, container last-termination reason, events, ConfigMaps or resource quotas could be read for checkout-service or payment-service in production-us-east-2; whether a config change, restart or resource shortfall occurred there is unknown. The query for Services in namespace app-269 returned status no_data (result_count 0), so service/endpoint configuration there is also unknown rather than shown healthy.

No data exists on stripe-us itself (no logs, health, status page or network telemetry), so whether the 30 s timeout came from the provider, from the egress path, or from payment-service's own client timeout cannot be determined; the named root cause is therefore recorded as partial.

The app-269-prod-logs index returned only 6 documents for the whole 24 h window and it is the only index present, so log completeness is unknown; whether the errors continued after the last ERROR document at 2026-11-21T06:08:55Z is not observable from this index.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so no record of configuration or deployment changes was available.
Secrets are not readable, so any API key/credential configuration for stripe-us could not be verified.

The previous container log stream of pod checkout-service-6d7f474c45-c7vkt was unavailable, so nothing from an earlier instance of that eu-west-2 pod could be read (it reports no previous terminated container).
next_steps: Confirm current impact: query app-269-prod-logs for cluster=production-us-east-2 after 2026-11-21T06:08:55Z and check whether checkout-service circuit-breaker errors continue.
Obtain stripe-us provider status and /v1/charges latency for 2026-11-21T04:00-06:30Z, and test egress from production-us-east-2 payment-service to stripe-us.

Read production-us-east-2 payment-service and checkout-service deployment env/config (upstream URL, retry, timeout, circuit-breaker threshold) and pod logs/events to confirm no cluster-side change coincided with 04:38:55Z.
Restore or provide Prometheus and Jaeger access so the 41% failure rate and any latency shift can be verified against a comparable baseline.
